title: Tenant cold-cache & blindspot observability playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a practical observability plan specifically targeted at tenant cold-cache events and the ‘blindspots’ they create for multi-tenant inference. Goal is to have a compact signal inventory, dashboard wireframes, tracing anchoring strategy, and a short investigation runbook operators can use during spikes that look like cache churn.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs on-call for inference runtime, serving-runtime engineers, platform product managers, solutions engineers who triage tenant incidents.
- Scope: hosted + dedicated backends; covers per-tenant cache heat, cache-miss amplification into latency/cost, and downstream error patterns triggered by cache storms (rate-limits, OOMs, degraded model fallbacks).

Background / Why this matters (short):
- We see recurring incidents where a small number of tenants (or even a single noisy job) cause widespread tail-latency regressions because of cold KV cache churn.
- Standard aggregate SLIs hide this: p50/p95 look okay while p99 spikes for affected tenants.
- Blindspots: dashboards often aggregate by model or region but not by tenant+cache-warmth, making triage slower.

Signal inventory (compact):
- tenant.kv_cache.hit_rate (percent): per-tenant rolling 1m/5m. Definition: hits / (hits+misses). Cardinality: tenant_id. Owner: caching-service. Suggested alert: tenant < 10% sustained for 2m AND token rate > baseline.
- tenant.request.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99): per-tenant. Definition: end-to-end serving time excluding client-side. Owner: runtime. Dash widgets: heatmap of tenants by p95.
- tenant.kv_cache.evictions_per_min (count): spikes indicate churn.
- tenant.token_cost_per_min (tokens/min): correlate cost jumps to cache misses.
- global.batch_size_distribution (histogram): to detect fallback to singleton inference.
- span.kv_cache.lookup.duration_ms (trace): span-level timing for KV lookups, label with hit/miss.
- span.model.load.duration_ms (trace): detect model reloads triggered by eviction/rollout.
- tenant.error.rate (5xx, 429): rate by tenant. Useful to spot cascading failures when cache misses overload model nodes.
- tenant.replayable_prompt_fraction (ratio): portion of requests that are deterministic replays (used for prompt-replay debugging).

Metric definition examples (copy-paste friendly):
- Metric name: tenant.kv_cache.hit_rate
  - Unit: percent (0-100)
  - Aggregation: max by tenant over 1m for alerting; mean by model for dashboards
  - Collection: counters kv_cache.hits and kv_cache.misses tagged with tenant_id; compute rate over 1m
  - Cardinality: tenant_id (high-cardinality); rollup strategy: only surface top-200 tenants in dashboard, and provide scatterplot full cardinality with sampling

Tracing and span design notes:
- Correlation keys: include tenant_id, session_id, request_id, and sampled_call_path in every top-level span. Make sure tenant_id is normalized and limited length.
- KV cache spans must emit a boolean tag: kv_cache_hit: true|false, and item_age_seconds when miss is true.
- Recommendation: instrument 'cache-priming' code path with a separate span name (cache.priming) so we can distinguish proactive background warms from on-request warms.
- Trace sampling: adopt severity-weighted sampling: always sample traces for requests where tenant.kv_cache.hit_rate < 20% OR latency_p99 > threshold OR error count > 0 in last 1m. For the rest, use low-rate head-based sampling (0.5%).
- Trace size guardrails: cap stored trace span count to 200 and redact large prompt payloads; store prompt hashes for replay only when request is flagged by ops.

Dashboard ideas / wireframes (for a single-page focused view):
Top row (triage quick-hit):
- Tenant p95 heatmap (rows=tenant groups, columns=time buckets 1m) — color by delta from baseline
- Top 10 tenants by kv_cache miss amplification (miss_rate * request_rate)
- Global token-cost burn vs expected baseline (1h/24h)

Middle row (drilldown):
- Time series: selected-tenant request latency p50/p95/p99 + overlaid kv_cache.hit_rate (dual axis)
 - Scatter: request size vs latency colored by kv_cache_hit boolean
- Bar: evictions_per_min by AZ/host to detect noisy hosts causing cross-tenant effects

Bottom row (correlation and traces):
- Table: recent traces for tenant filtered by kv_cache_hit=false with links to trace viewer and prompt excerpt (hashed)
- Alerts panel: active alerts for tenant groups + suggested remediation checklist

Alerting guidance (starter):
- Tenant cold-cache alert: (tenant.kv_cache.hit_rate < 15% for 2m) AND (tenant.request.rate > baseline * 2) -> P2, notify #ops-inference with tenant tag
- Tenant cost surge: (token_cost_per_min > baseline * 3 for 5m) -> P3, notify owner
- Miss amplification global: (top-5 tenants miss_amplification sum > 40% of region traffic) -> P1, auto-run basic mitigation (throttle lowest-priority tenant requests, route to warmed pools)

Investigation runbook (short):
1) Identify tenant(s) from heatmap or alert.
2) Check tenant.kv_cache.evictions_per_min and host-level eviction spikes. If evictions spike, find host(s) and inspect host memory pressure metrics.
3) Open trace viewer for recent traces with kv_cache_hit=false. Look for long model.load spans or repeated cache priming.
4) If model nodes overloaded: consider temporary routing to degraded model (fallback) or increase burst capacity (Dedicated) if configured.
5) If tenant is noisy (e.g., replays or large-batch jobs), contact solutions-eng for rate-limiting or quota adjustments.
6) Document incident: add root cause hypothesis and assign follow-up (e.g., lock per-tenant cache lanes, bump warm thresholds).

Playbook mitigation knobs (quick list):
- soft throttle for tenant (token-based)
- increase per-tenant cache reservations on heavy tenants (if dedicated)
- divert some requests to warmed read-replicas or fallbacks
- on-service: trigger background priming job for affected tenant using sample prompts (short-term)

Operational constraints and cost-aware decisions:
- We cannot keep full per-tenant high-cardinality dashboards for > 30k tenants; default rollups + top-n widgets needed.
- Traces for every cache miss are too expensive; use severity-weighted sampling and always-sample when alerts trigger to get root cause.

Open questions / tradeoffs (for engineering discussion):
- Do we want a per-tenant cached-reservation quota that autosizes? Operational complexity vs predictability.
- How aggressive should automatic throttling be for high-amplification tenants? Risk: false positives affecting legitimate bursty workloads.
- Can we safely store prompt hashes for replay without violating PII rules? Need security review (see linked_artifacts).

Next steps / action items (owner -> due):
- Build dashboard prototype (Liam Chen) -> 2024-11-09
- Implement severity-weighted trace sampling rules (Ravi Sundaram) -> 2024-11-16
- Create templated incident runbook snippet and add to oncall playbooks (Mariana Gomez) -> 2024-11-02
- Security review for prompt-hash storage (Asha Patel) -> 2024-11-15

Notes / scratchpad (things to try):
- Try a synthetic probe that warms cache for top-100 tenants once per 10m and measure improvement in p99.
- Small experiment: when miss rate > 40% for tenant and host memory > 80%, route new tenant requests to warm pool for 10s and log effect.

References and shortcuts:
- Related: JIRA-7893 (tenant cache incident postmortem)
- Telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/456

Unresolved (TODOs before rolling to prod):
- Finalize sampling rates and implement guard rails to stop trace billing explosion.
- Decide retention policy for prompt-hash map and access controls.

End of playbook - feedback welcome.
